summary: Vyakti GroupAI (/home/user/vyakti-groupai; branches main@d06efdc 3 commits, codex/relational-core@4bae159 40, claude/vyakti-cloning-platform-aq05n4@451de5a 43 = codex + 2 Claude fixes for migration 019) is the trust kernel for an 'AI common friend': one AI identity with distinct relationships to each person, dyad and group, which may bridge private info into a group only through explicit, scoped, revocable grants, and whose success is measured by human-human outcomes (Commitment Keeper), with silence first-class. Architecture: append-only social event ledger per 'social world' (RLS on world_id), immutable audience epochs, cited memories with versioned DisclosurePolicy (purposes, acts influence/gist/paraphrase/verbatim, obligations, deny-wins), derivation that cannot declassify, authorization before any plaintext reaches a model, an authorization-issued Context Capsule with whole-block budgets and manifest hash, a deterministic non-LLM intervention policy, and durable Postgres machinery (fenced head-of-line turns, model request ledger where timeouts become 'ambiguous' and are reconciled not retried, delivery lanes, shared/exclusive per-world privacy barrier, cryptographic erasure). 12 TS packages (~41k lines incl. tests) + 19 migrations (17.4k SQL lines) + 7.3k lines of SQL verifies, built in 6 days (2026-08-30..09-04). Evidence: 375/375 local tests; hosted CI run 33758157417 applied/verified 001-019 and passed 17/17 runtime integrations; Neon PG18 proof only for 001-013; synthetic Campaigns 0/0B/0C (960 worlds, 3,120 assertions) at zero violations. I replicated all three campaigns from source with Taxila's own tsc 7.0.2 + zod 4.6.5 and ran a 50,000-case differential of authorizeDisclosure against an independently written oracle: 0 mismatches, plus a REAL negative control (deny-ignoring evaluator caught 799 times) because the repo's own negative controls are tautological. Nothing is deployed: no UI, channel adapter, production provider, KMS, composition root or human pilot; Campaign 1 is shadow-only and hard NO-SHIP. The branch name says 'cloning platform' but contains no voice/TTS/avatar code. It is adult-only by construction (adultOnly literal, adultAttested consent), which Taxila must invert to guardian consent. Portable now: relational-core, intervention-policy, context-capsule, simulator compile cleanly with Taxila's toolchain and can be vendored; pilot-telemetry, follow-through-core reminders, model-gateway and delivery-runtime are adapt-grade; postgres-runtime and migrations 014-019 should be mined for patterns, not depended on. Key caveat for Vercel+Neon: the privacy barrier needs a direct session connection (not pooler/HTTP). The highest-value harvest is the 48-node failure log (Postgres parameter/column shadowing that made revoked consent look current, JSONB null, sparse-array unanimity bypass, lock-upgrade deadlock, BYPASSRLS Neon roles).
